elements.quote: Point-of-care ultrasound improves clinical outcomes in patients with acute onset dyspnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis
elements.reason: The report is explicitly identified as a systematic review and meta-analysis in the title associated with the abstract.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of the use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (PoCUS) versus conventional management on clinical outcomes in patients with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective explicitly.

elements.quote: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and prospective and retrospective cohort studies that compared PoCUS with conventional diagnostic modalities (controls) in patients with acute onset dyspnea were included.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the main inclusion criteria (study designs, comparison, population).

elements.quote: The Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, EMBASE and reference lists were searched to identify eligible trials (inception to October 14, 2021).
elements.reason: Information sources and the last search date are reported in the abstract.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers extracted data and assessed the risk of bias.
elements.reason: The abstract states that risk of bias was assessed by two independent reviewers but does not specify the tools/methods used (e.g., RoB 2, ROBINS-I).

elements.quote: Time to diagnosis (mean difference [MD], - 63 min; 95% CI, - 115 to - 11 min] and time to treatment (MD, - 27 min; 95% CI - 43 to - 11 min) were significantly shorter in the PoCUS group.
elements.reason: Meta-analytic synthesis is implied by reporting of pooled mean differences and odds ratios with confidence intervals, but the methods of presentation/synthesis are not explicitly described in the abstract.

elements.quote: We included eight RCTs and six observational studies with a total of 5393 participants.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants with study design characteristics.

elements.quote: The primary study outcomes were time to diagnosis, time to treatment, and length of stay (LOS). Secondary outcomes included rate of appropriate treatment, 30-day re-admission rate, and mortality.
elements.reason: The abstract defines and reports results for the main outcomes.

elements.quote: Time to diagnosis (mean difference [MD], - 63 min; 95% CI, - 115 to - 11 min] and time to treatment (MD, - 27 min; 95% CI - 43 to - 11 min)
elements.reason: The abstract reports summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals for the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Patients in the PoCUS group showed significantly higher odds of receiving appropriate therapy compared to controls (odds ratio [OR], 2.31; 95% CI, 1.61-3.32)
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group is favored (e.g., shorter times and higher odds in the PoCUS group).

elements.quote: with overall low or moderate study quality and low or moderate risk of bias (except one article with serious risk of bias)
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes limitations regarding study quality and risk of bias.

elements.quote: Our results indicate that PoCUS use contributes to early diagnosis and better outcomes compared to conventional methods in patients admitted with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not mention any funding source; funding appears only in the body text (text_22), not in the abstract.
The abstract does not report the registry name or registration number; PROSPERO registration (CRD42021284070) appears only in the methods section (text_5).

elements.quote: Even given all these tests, some studies have raised doubts about the diagnostic accuracy of these conventional approaches, especially in the critically ill patient population [13, 14].
elements.reason: The Introduction describes current knowledge (conventional diagnostic workup, its limitations, high mortality) and the uncertainty regarding diagnostic accuracy, motivating the review.

elements.quote: Therefore, we conducted a high-quality, comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis that included the most recent publications that reported clinical outcomes with the use of PoCUS in patients who developed acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The need for the review is explicitly explained: rapid diagnosis is of utmost importance, conventional approaches have doubtful accuracy, and few trials have examined clinical outcomes (text_3: 'very few trials have examined meaningful clinical outcomes related to PoCUS usage to date').

elements.quote: In addition to the existing diagnostic accuracy studies [16-20, 25], our main objective, as a new insight to this field, was to investigate how PoCUS improves clinical endpoints in patients with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: Existing reviews/diagnostic accuracy studies are cited and the distinct need for the current review (clinical outcomes vs diagnostic accuracy) is explained; text_19 further contrasts with previous reviews [16-20, 60].

elements.quote: PoCUS has other advantages, such as being free from ionizing radiation, and most importantly can be performed in real-time at the bedside [16, 21]. Additionally, PoCUS can answer a broad spectrum of remaining diagnostic questions and may also help to optimize and personalize therapy [22].
elements.reason: The mechanism by which PoCUS may improve outcomes (real-time bedside imaging enabling faster diagnosis and therapy optimization) is briefly described in the introduction.
This is a review of a diagnostic intervention (PoCUS) rather than a complex multi-component intervention or delivery context; no logic model requirement applies and none is reported.

elements.quote: our main objective, as a new insight to this field, was to investigate how PoCUS improves clinical endpoints in patients with acute onset dyspnea. O: For the primary outcomes, we defined time to diagnosis ... time to treatment ... and length of stay (LOS) ... The secondary outcomes were the following: mortality (in-hospital and 30-day), rate of appropriate treatment and 30-day re-admission rate.
elements.reason: The Introduction explicitly states the review objective and defines primary and secondary outcomes.

elements.quote: The selected studies had to match our previously defined PICO (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome) framework ... P: Adults and children who were admitted to the ED or to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) ... I: The examined intervention was PoCUS use on its own or in combination with conventional diagnostic measures ... C: Control group included conventional diagnostic methods
elements.reason: Planned comparison is stated using PICO: population and intervention in text_7, control in text_7, and outcomes in text_4.

elements.quote: The selected studies had to match our previously defined PICO (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome) framework... P: Adults and children who were admitted to the ED or to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), or to another inpatient setting because of acute onset or worsening dyspnea were eligible... Studies reporting on trauma-induced acute onset dyspnea, or pregnancy were excluded. I: The examined intervention was PoCUS use on its own or in combination with conventional diagnostic measures... C: Control group included conventional diagnostic methods, such as taking the patients' medical history, physical examination, ECG, blood gas and different laboratory analyses, echocardiography, CXR, or computer tomography (CT).
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria are specified via a PICO framework covering population, setting, intervention, comparator, and eligible study designs (text_6: RCTs and prospective/retrospective cohort studies).

elements.quote: We did not use any restrictions or limitations based on language or publication date.
elements.reason: Report characteristics are addressed: no language or publication date restrictions; text_6 specifies publication status (excluding editorials, conference abstracts, non-peer-reviewed articles).
No evidence distinguishes exclusion of studies because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and prospective and retrospective cohort studies that compared PoCUS with conventional diagnostic modalities (controls) in patients with acute onset dyspnea were included... The primary study outcomes were time to diagnosis, time to treatment, and length of stay (LOS). Secondary outcomes included rate of appropriate treatment, 30-day re-admission rate, and mortality.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (PoCUS vs conventional diagnostic controls) are specified and linked to the review objective and outcome-based syntheses (time to diagnosis, LOS, mortality, etc.).
Restrictions (e.g., excluding trauma-induced dyspnea or pregnancy) are stated but no rationales for these notable restrictions are provided.

elements.quote: We systematically searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for eligible articles on 14 October, 2021.
elements.reason: The last search date (14 October 2021) is explicitly reported for all databases searched.

elements.reason: A study register (CENTRAL) was searched and it is stated that no date restrictions were applied.

elements.quote: two review authors (G.S. and C.S.) independently screened titles, abstracts, and then the full texts

No evidence of contacting investigators to obtain or confirm eligibility information; no indication this was done.

elements.quote: were extracted by two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.) using our standardized data collection form in Microsoft Excel

elements.quote: In the case of one study (Blans [46]), the author kindly provided the original data on patients with dyspnea, excluding all other causes.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports obtaining data from a study investigator (original data provided by the Blans study author), though this is described in the Discussion rather than Methods.
No automation tools used in data collection are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: extracting numerical data from figures was particularly difficult
elements.reason: The authors acknowledge extracting data from figures, but no software used for figure data extraction is specified.

elements.quote: There were no overlapping populations or duplicate data.

elements.quote: the available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted by two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.) using our standardized data collection form in Microsoft Excel.
elements.reason: The Methods data-collection description does not list or define the outcome domains; outcomes (time to diagnosis, time to treatment, LOS in hospital/ED/ICU, appropriate therapy, 30-day re-admission, mortality) are only identifiable from the Results sections (text_8, text_9), not formally listed and defined in the Methods.
No time frame of measurement is specified for any outcome domain in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results (measures, time points, analyses) within each outcome domain were sought.

elements.quote: There was no deviation from the protocol.

elements.quote: Data on the first author, publication year, countries, study design, number of patients in each group and their baseline characteristics (including age and gender), type of PoCUS protocol, examiners' practice and the available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted by two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.) using our standardized data collection form in Microsoft Excel.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists and defines all variables sought (bibliographic details, study design, patient characteristics, PoCUS protocol, examiner practice, and outcomes) collected via a standardized data collection form.

elements.quote: If the mean and SD were not reported in the article, we estimated them from the medians, quartiles, minimum and maximums using the Luo [32] and Shi [33] methods.
elements.reason: The authors describe assumptions and methods for handling missing or unclear study information (estimating means/SDs from reported medians/quartiles/ranges); text_19 further notes handling of unclear data (e.g., extracting data from figures, a 21-day re-admission period instead of 30 days).

elements.quote: Based on the consensus of methodological and clinical experts, we created a standardized data collection sheet.
elements.reason: No external tool was used to determine which data items to collect; the data collection form was developed by the authors themselves, so no tool citation applies.
